Visit note | 2025-12-14 04:00 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Obaidul Talukder, 58, male. Mr. Talukder attends for review regarding his knee. He reports pain when using stairs, morning stiffness lasting a few minutes, and a noticeable creaking in the joint. He is a mobile phone repair technician and notes his discomfort became worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Bogura. He presents with a sudden locking of the knee with little pain. He is a mobile phone repair technician. He has no known chronic comorbidity. Examination reveals BMI 28.2, BP 136/70 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 52 kg. Joint inspection shows mild crepitus on movement with stable ligaments. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice given: do thigh-strengthening exercises daily; lose weight; avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up: 6 weeks with physiotherapy.
